claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is a chemically disordered BCC solid solution.
Atomic-size mismatch produces high lattice distortion in disordered HfNbTaTiZr.
Controlled annealing or Monte Carlo treatment can induce chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced short-range order preferentially forms HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
HfTi and TiZr clusters can percolate and nucleate coherent B2-like ordered precipitates in HfNbTaTiZr.
Ordered B2-like domains and percolating SRO clusters reduce local strain fields and RMS lattice distortion relative to the random HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Reducing local strain fields decreases the scattering rate of high-frequency phonons.
The reduction in high-frequency phonon scattering increases the lattice thermal conductivity of ordered HfNbTaTiZr relative to its random state.
Coherent B2 clusters are phonon-transparent and provide percolative heat-transport pathways rather than acting as scattering centers.
The proposed conductivity enhancement requires cluster sizes below the phonon mean free path.
In random alloys, atomic-size mismatch produces local lattice distortion that Rayleigh-scatters high-frequency phonons.
B2 ordering permits atoms to occupy lower-energy, more symmetric positions and thereby reduces strain-field amplitude.
The cited MoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloy exhibits a driving force for chemical short-range ordering.
B2-like structures have been observed in MoNbTaW.
Ordered B2 phases and B2-plus-BCC decomposition occur in at least some high-entropy alloy systems and depend on composition and annealing temperature.
The reduction in distortion-related scattering can outweigh scattering introduced by ordered-domain or phase boundaries.
Lattice thermal conductivity varies non-monotonically with SRO, initially increasing and reaching a maximum when a percolating B2 network forms.
Further coarsening or conversion to incoherent precipitates decreases lattice thermal conductivity through interface scattering.
Ordering reduces the broadening of high-frequency optical-phonon DOS features associated with local distortion.
The conductivity-increase regime requires coherent B2 clusters smaller than 10–20 nm, whereas incoherent phase separation produces sufficient thermal-boundary resistance to decrease conductivity.
